title: Make Your First Commit
description: Stage and save a change with git — the foundation of working on any team codebase.

steps.instruction: In your repo, run `git status` to see what's changed
hints: You'll see modified files in red and any untracked files at the bottom

steps.instruction: Open any file in the repo and make a small edit — even a blank line is fine
hints: Save the file once you've edited it
Re-run `git status` to confirm git sees the change

steps.instruction: Stage your change with `git add <filename>` (or `git add .` for everything)
hints: `git add .` stages every change in the current directory
`git status` will now show the file in green

steps.instruction: Run `git commit -m "your message"` — write a short description of the change
hints: Good messages use imperative mood: 'Add login button', not 'Added login button'
Under 72 characters is a good target

steps.instruction: Run `git log -1` to confirm your commit is recorded
hints: You should see your commit at the top with your name and message
